key_insight: A U-Net predicts full 36-component 3D strain localization fields, with network width and depth emerging as the key scaling parameters.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate can accelerate repeated mechanical-field computations in concrete mesostructures, supporting computational homogenization and multiscale simulation.
method: Train on localization tensors generated by an FFT-based linear elastic solver at voxel resolutions up to 256³.
Optimize U-Net hyperparameters to identify architecture scaling rules and accuracy–speed trade-offs.
Use Maximum Mean Discrepancy on internal feature maps to flag out-of-distribution microstructures without reference simulations.
evidence_signal: The final model reports 1.118% mean absolute error on both validation and held-out test sets and approximately 8.7× faster inference than the FFT solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU.
watch_item: Generalization depends on morphological diversity in training; transfer across aggregate volume fractions does not establish reliability for arbitrary microstructures.
paper_title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
